summary.headline: Cyient DLM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34.3% YoY to INR3,738 million, with a record INR25,989 million order book and 10.5% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 34.3% YoY to INR3,738 million and normalized PAT more than doubled to INR163 million, with PAT margin at 4.4%. Order intake was INR551.9 million-equivalent per the call (INR551.9 crores) at a 1.5x book-to-bill, lifting the order book to a record INR25,989 million. Management flagged West Asia disruption (logistics delays and cost increases) as ongoing but said it was managed through inventory build. Working capital days rose to 161 from 145 QoQ, and free cash flow remained negative.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: 42% of Q1 FY27 revenue, growing 40% YoY. Management cites Honeywell and Thales ramps, with Honeywell builds expected to ramp over the next 18 months.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue, growing 90% YoY, making it the second-largest segment.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: 9% of revenue, growing 35% YoY; build-to-print momentum cited in North America and Europe.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue with broadly flat YoY growth, attributed to a seasonal customer impact; management guides the sales pipeline at 17-20% of revenue.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: PCBA 48% of revenue (+21% YoY); box build 21% (+85% YoY); mechanical and others 10%; cables 1%. Auto and others 1% of segment mix.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Rest of world 94% of revenue, India 6%. Management did not give USD-constant growth for ROW when asked.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 and subsequent quarters to show momentum similar to Q1 in revenue and order intake; no hard numeric guidance given.
Book-to-bill expected to stay around 1.5x for the full year.
Gross margin to stay slightly below Q4 FY26 levels due to budgeted organisation investments.
B2S product revenues expected to become substantial over the next 12-18 months; B2S adds 250-300 bps to consolidated EBITDA margin.
Expand phase (FY27-FY29) targets 11-13% EBITDA margin via robotics and AI data centre; Transform (FY30+) targets 13-18%.
Robotics and AI data centre order intake expected in FY27, with revenue contribution later (FY28-FY29); product detail to follow in 2-3 quarters.
Semiconductor capital equipment revenue growth expected over the next 6-12 months.
Capex about 1.75x-2x of revenue per management; no additional expansion capex beyond regular annual capex expected.
capex_capacity: Build-to-specifications lab expanded from 6,000 sq ft to 15,000 sq ft, more than doubling footprint.
Nadcap audit completed for cable harness assembly at Mysore unit.
ITAR-certified facility in North America in use for one US defence project, with more US defence prospects in pipeline.
Management says no additional expansion capex required for AI data centre and robotics; existing capabilities sufficient, with some application-engineering hires needed.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR25,989 million is the highest in company history; order intake drove 1.5x book-to-bill.
Two new logos added in Q1 across industrial and automotive.
Management says no lumpy one-off orders in the INR551.9 crore intake; about 70% of new-segment intake from existing customers and 30% from customers added in last 4-6 quarters.
Sales pipeline mix: about 48% aerospace and defence, under 40% industrial and semiconductor capital equipment, balance mainly MedTech, with automotive small.
Management declined to disclose total pipeline size; an analyst's INR4,000-5,000 crore figure was not confirmed.
Management cited Middle East/West Asia-related logistics delays and cost increases, but said no Q1 impact; Israel-related orders showed good intake with delays easing.

qa_highlights.question: Effect of the West Asia crisis and status of delayed Israeli approvals/orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisis ongoing; logistics delays and cost increases seen, but inventory pre-build and alternative sourcing meant no Q1 impact, with a Q2 plan in place. Israeli customer order intake was strong and momentum expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MedTech growth flat and how will it progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal impact from one customer; management sees no concern, with pipeline at 17-20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin decline QoQ despite higher revenue, and is there tariff reimbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin slightly lower QoQ due to budgeted investments in the organisation; no tariff reimbursement discussed. Momentum in Q2 expected to be similar.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there an FX loss and why is operating cash flow negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Rupee appreciated in the last month, and the balance sheet is exposed to large export and import flows. Negative FCF is from higher inventory and lower customer advances; management expects cash flow to turn positive once inventory is controlled.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company provide order-book or order-intake guidance for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance given; management said book-to-bill will stay around 1.5x for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How are aerospace and European defence trends, and what is the B2S timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Honeywell and Thales ramps are expected; management said aerospace is a hard-to-enter, sticky moat. A Japan eVTOL B2S program is 12-18 months from production, and a European defence build-to-spec engagement is at an early stage.

risks_watch: Negative free cash flow and net working capital days rising to 161 from 145 QoQ, driven by inventory of 162 days.
West Asia conflict causing logistics delays and cost increases; management says Q2 is planned for, but the situation is ongoing.
MedTech growth flat YoY in Q1 with a customer-related seasonal impact.
Gross margin lower QoQ; management attributes this to investments, and the margin contribution from new segments is not yet quantified.
AI data centre and robotics product details, customers and revenue split are still undisclosed; update promised in 2-3 quarters.
Customer advances dropped to 15 days from 18 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and the margin roadmap, but evasive on specifics: product lines for AI data centre and robotics, pipeline size, USD-constant ROW growth and full-year order guidance were all deferred. Cautious on West Asia, which management says is still ongoing.
key_quotes: We closed the quarter with the highest ever order book in the company's history, providing strong revenue visibility and reaffirming customer confidence in our capabilities.
So, book-to-bill ratio will be at the same thing where we are today at 1.5x. So, we will be at that number for the year too.
As I said, we don't need any additional capex for that.
